questions.knowledgeNote: cosx = +-1/2: read both branches off the unit circle - pi/3 in QI/QIV.
questions.question: Q1(a). Solve 4cos^2x = 1.
questions.solution: cos^2x = 1/4, so cosx = 1/2 or cosx = -1/2. Both give x = n.pi +- pi/3. Matches the printed Answers key (p154): 'n.pi +- pi/3'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q1(a); book p152 = PDF p179 (OCR conf 0.93); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos2x = 1 - 2sin^2x turns it into a quadratic in sinx: (2sinx-1)(sinx+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q1(b). Solve cos2x - sinx = 0.
questions.solution: 1-2sin^2x-sinx = 0, i.e. 2sin^2x+sinx-1 = (2sinx-1)(sinx+1) = 0. sinx = 1/2: x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6. sinx = -1: x = 2n.pi-pi/2 (=(4n-1).pi/2). Both verified by substitution.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q1(b); book p152 = PDF p179; key form differs, answers verified

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2x = 2sinxcosx: factor sinx out and solve each factor.
questions.question: Q1(c). Solve 2sin2x = sinx.
questions.solution: 4sinxcosx-sinx = sinx(4cosx-1) = 0. sinx = 0: x = n.pi. cosx = 1/4: x = 2n.pi +- cos^(-1)(1/4). Matches the key: 'n.pi, 2n.pi +- cos^(-1)(1/4)'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q1(c); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Same factor trick: sinx(2cosx+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q1(d). Solve sin2x + sinx = 0.
questions.solution: sinx(2cosx+1) = 0. sinx = 0: x = n.pi. cosx = -1/2: x = 2n.pi +- 2pi/3 (=(6n+-2).pi/3). Matches the key: 'n.pi, (6n+-2).pi/3'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q1(d); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin^2 = 1 - cos^2: the equation becomes cosx(cosx+1) = 0 - handle BOTH branches.
questions.question: Q2(a). Solve sin^2x - cosx = 1.
questions.solution: (1-cos^2x)-cosx = 1 gives cosx(cosx+1) = 0. cosx = 0: x = (4n+-1).pi/2. cosx = -1: x = (2n+1).pi. (Note: x = (2n+1).pi/2 alone would wrongly admit x = pi; both families are needed.) Matches the key.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q2(a); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Quadratic in sinx with roots -3 and 2: both outside [-1,1], so no solution exists.
questions.question: Q2(b). Solve cos^2x - sinx + 5 = 0.
questions.solution: (1-sin^2x)-sinx+5 = 0 gives sin^2x+sinx-6 = (sinx+3)(sinx-2) = 0. sinx = -3 or 2 are both impossible. No solution. Matches the key: 'No solution'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q2(b); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by cosx: a perfect square (2cosx-1)^2 = 0 - a double root.
questions.question: Q2(c). Solve 4cosx + secx - 4 = 0.
questions.solution: 4cos^2x-4cosx+1 = (2cosx-1)^2 = 0, so cosx = 1/2: x = 2n.pi +- pi/3 (=(6n+-1).pi/3). Matches the key.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q2(c); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by sinx, then REJECT cosx = 1: it makes cot/cosec undefined in the original.
questions.question: Q2(d). Solve 2sinx + cotx - cosecx = 0.
questions.solution: 2sin^2x+cosx-1 = 0 gives 2cos^2x-cosx-1 = (2cosx+1)(cosx-1) = 0. cosx = 1 would make sinx = 0 (cot, cosec undefined) - rejected. cosx = -1/2: x = 2n.pi +- 2pi/3. Matches the key: '(6n+-2).pi/3' (rejection noted).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q2(d); book p152 = PDF p179; matches key; extraneous root rejected

questions.knowledgeNote: 2+2sin^2x = 3 at once: sin^2x = 1/2.
questions.question: Q3(a). Solve 2cos^2x + 4sin^2x = 3.
questions.solution: 2(1-sin^2x)+4sin^2x = 3 gives 2sin^2x = 1, sinx = +-1/sqrt(2): x = n.pi +- pi/4. Matches the key. (Statement order confirmed by 200-dpi image read.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q3(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.question: Q3(b). Solve 7sin^2x + 3cos^2x = 4.
questions.solution: 4sin^2x+3(cos^2x+sin^2x)... = 4sin^2x+3 = 4, so sin^2x = 1/4, sinx = +-1/2: x = n.pi +- pi/6. Verified: x = pi/6 gives 7/4+3(3/4) = 7/4+9/4 = 4. (Statement via image read.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q3(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: tan+cot = 1/(sinxcosx): the sinx cancels leaving cosx = 1/2 (sinx = 0 was never allowed).
questions.question: Q3(c). Solve tanx + cotx = 2cosecx.
questions.solution: (sin^2x+cos^2x)/(sinxcosx) = 2/sinx gives 1/cosx = 2 (sinx != 0), so cosx = 1/2: x = 2n.pi +- pi/3. Verified: tan(pi/3)+cot(pi/3) = sqrt(3)+1/sqrt(3) = 4/sqrt(3) = 2cosec(pi/3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q3(c); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: tan^2 = sec^2-1: (secx-2)(secx+1) = 0 - and secx = -1 (x = odd pi) IS valid here since tan is 0, not undefined.
questions.question: Q3(d). Solve tan^2x = secx + 1 [HSEB 2058].
questions.solution: sec^2x-1 = secx+1 gives (secx-2)(secx+1) = 0. secx = 2: x = 2n.pi +- pi/3. secx = -1: x = (2n+1).pi (tan = 0, sec = -1: 0 = -1+1 checks). Matches the key: '(2n+1).pi, 2n.pi +- ...'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q3(d) [HSEB 2058]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: R-form: sinx+sqrt(3)cosx = 2sin(x+pi/3) = sqrt(2).
questions.question: Q4(a). Solve sinx + sqrt(3)cosx = sqrt(2) [T.U. 2049 H] [HSEB 2055].
questions.solution: 2sin(x+pi/3) = sqrt(2), so sin(x+pi/3) = 1/sqrt(2): x+pi/3 = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/4, i.e. x = 2n.pi-pi/12 or 2n.pi+5pi/12. Verified: x = -pi/12 gives sin(-pi/12)+sqrt(3)cos(-pi/12) = sqrt(2). (Statement via image read.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q4(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: 2sin(x-pi/6) = sqrt(2) with x-pi/6 in [-pi/6, 5pi/6]: only pi/4 and 3pi/4 qualify.
questions.question: Q4(b). Solve sqrt(3)sinx - cosx = sqrt(2) (0 <= x <= pi).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q4(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); both values verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Same equation as Q4(a) (addition commutes) - same solution set; the book asks it twice (once as T.U. 2053).
questions.question: Q4(c). Solve cosx + sqrt(3)sinx = sqrt(2) [T.U. 2053].
questions.solution: Identical to Q4(a) (terms commute): x = 2n.pi-pi/12 or 2n.pi+5pi/12. (Duplication is in the print, kept faithfully.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q4(c) [T.U. 2053]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sqrt(2)sin(x+pi/4) = sqrt(2) forces sin = 1: x = 2n.pi+pi/4, then keep only those inside [-2pi, 2pi].
questions.question: Q4(d). Solve sinx + cosx = sqrt(2) (-2pi <= x <= 2pi).
questions.solution: sin(x+pi/4) = 1 gives x = 2n.pi+pi/4. Inside [-2pi, 2pi]: n = -1 gives -7pi/4; n = 0 gives pi/4 (n = 1 gives 9pi/4 > 2pi, excluded). Solutions: x = -7pi/4, pi/4. Both verified.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q4(d); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); interval filter applied

questions.knowledgeNote: sin3x+sinx = 2sin2xcosx: the cosx factor is absorbed - everything is already covered by sin2x = 0.
questions.question: Q5(a). Solve sin3x + sinx = 0.
questions.solution: 2sin2xcosx = 0. sin2x = 0: x = n.pi/2 (this already includes cosx = 0's (2n+1).pi/2). So x = n.pi/2. Verified: x = pi/2 gives sin(3pi/2)+sin(pi/2) = -1+1 = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q5(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Move sin2x over: sin2x(2cosx-1) = 0.
questions.question: Q5(b). Solve sin3x + sinx = sin2x.
questions.solution: 2sin2xcosx-sin2x = sin2x(2cosx-1) = 0. sin2x = 0: x = n.pi/2. cosx = 1/2: x = 2n.pi +- pi/3. Verified: x = pi/3 gives sin(pi)+sin(pi/3) = sqrt(3)/2 = sin(2pi/3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q5(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: cos3x-cosx = -2sin2xsinx: the extra sinx factor adds nothing beyond sin2x = 0.
questions.question: Q5(c). Solve cos3x - cosx = 0.
questions.solution: -2sin2xsinx = 0. sin2x = 0: x = n.pi/2 (includes sinx = 0's n.pi). So x = n.pi/2. Verified: x = pi/2 gives cos(3pi/2)-cos(pi/2) = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q5(c); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: 3x = n.pi with the window (-pi/2, pi/2): only -pi/3, 0, pi/3 survive (endpoints and +-pi/4 were never in the set).
questions.question: Q5(d). Solve tan2x + tanx = 0 (-pi/2 <= x <= pi/2).
questions.solution: tan2x = tan(-x) gives 2x = n.pi-x, i.e. x = n.pi/3. In [-pi/2, pi/2] with tan defined: x = -pi/3, 0, pi/3 (each verified: tan(-2pi/3)+tan(-pi/3) = -sqrt(3)+... = 0). Endpoints +-pi/2 excluded (tan undefined).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q5(d); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); interval filter applied

questions.knowledgeNote: Divide by cos^2x: tan^2x-tanx-2 = (tanx-2)(tanx+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q6(a). Solve 2cos^2x + sinxcosx - sin^2x = 0.
questions.solution: 2+tanx-tan^2x = 0, i.e. (tanx-2)(tanx+1) = 0. tanx = 2: x = n.pi+alpha (alpha = tan^(-1)2). tanx = -1: x = n.pi-pi/4. Matches the key: 'n.pi-pi/4, n.pi+alpha'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q6(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Group as 2sinx(cosx-2)-(cosx-2): cosx = 2 is impossible, leaving sinx = 1/2.
questions.question: Q6(b). Solve sin2x - 4sinx - cosx + 2 = 0.
questions.solution: (2sinx-1)(cosx-2) = 0. cosx = 2 impossible. sinx = 1/2: x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6. Verified: x = pi/6 gives sin(pi/3)-4(1/2)-cos(pi/6)+2 = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q6(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: 9theta = n.pi+(-1)^n.theta: even n gives theta = mpi/4, odd n gives (2m+1).pi/10 - check each branch, don't just write n.pi/8.
questions.question: Q7(a). Solve sin9theta = sintheta.
questions.solution: 9theta = n.pi+(-1)^n.theta. n even (n = 2m): 8theta = 2m.pi, theta = m.pi/4. n odd: 10theta = (2m+1).pi, theta = (2m+1).pi/10. Verified: theta = pi/4 gives sin(9pi/4) = sin(pi/4); theta = pi/10 gives sin(9pi/10) = sin(pi/10).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q7(a); book p153 = PDF p180; branches derived exactly

questions.knowledgeNote: cot2theta = tan(pi/2-2theta): linear equation 7theta = n.pi+pi/2.
questions.question: Q7(b). Solve tan5theta = cot2theta.
questions.solution: 5theta = n.pi+(pi/2-2theta), so 7theta = n.pi+pi/2: theta = (2n+1).pi/14. Verified: theta = pi/14 gives tan(5pi/14) = cot(pi/7).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q7(b); book p153 = PDF p180; verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: tan2x = tan(pi/2-x): 3x = n.pi+pi/2 - and every one of these keeps both tans defined.
questions.question: Q7(c). Solve tan2x - cotx = 0.
questions.solution: 2x = n.pi+(pi/2-x), so x = (2n+1).pi/6. Definedness: (2n+1).pi/6 = pi/2+k.pi would need 2n+1 = 3+6k (odd = odd: n = 1+3k gives x = pi/2 mod pi - but tan(pi) = 0 and cot(pi/2) = 0 are both DEFINED, value 0-0 = 0, valid!). All x = (2n+1).pi/6 valid; never hits tan2x's pi/4+k.pi/2 (would need even = odd) or cot's k.pi. Verified at pi/6, pi/2, 5pi/6.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q7(c); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); definedness checked

questions.knowledgeNote: tan(m.theta) = tan(n.theta-pi/2): (m-n).theta = k.pi-pi/2. If m = n the equation is 1/(sin.cos) = 0 - impossible.
questions.question: Q7(d). Solve tan(m.theta) + cot(n.theta) = 0.
questions.solution: tan(m.theta) = -cot(n.theta) = tan(n.theta-pi/2), so (m-n).theta = k.pi-pi/2: theta = (2k-1).pi/(2(m-n)) for m != n (wherever all tans/cots are defined). If m = n: tan+cot = 1/(sin.cos) = 0 has no solution. (Standard form; validity caveat as stated.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q7(d); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); m = n case noted

questions.knowledgeNote: Pair outer terms: cos+cos3 = 2cos2cos - then cos2theta factors the whole row.
questions.question: Q8(a). Solve costheta + cos2theta + cos3theta = 0 [T.U. 2056 S].
questions.solution: (cos+cos3)+cos2 = 2cos2.cos+cos2 = cos2(2cos+1) = 0. cos2 = 0: theta = n.pi +- pi/4 (=(4n+-1).pi/4). cos = -1/2: theta = 2n.pi +- 2pi/3 (=(6n+-2).pi/3). Matches the key's three-family form.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q8(a) [T.U. 2056 S]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos-cos2 = -2sin(3t/2)sin(-t/2): three families - 2n.pi/3, n.pi+pi/4, 2n.pi-pi/2.
questions.question: Q8(b). Solve costheta - sin3theta = cos2theta.
questions.solution: cos-cos2 = sin3 gives 2sin(3t/2)sin(t/2) = 2sin(3t/2)cos(3t/2), i.e. 2sin(3t/2)(sin(t/2)-cos(3t/2)) = 0. sin(3t/2) = 0: t = 2n.pi/3. Else sin(t/2) = cos(3t/2) = sin(pi/2-3t/2): t = n.pi+pi/4 or t = 2n.pi-pi/2 (even/odd-n branches). All three verified (e.g. t = -pi/2: 0-1 = -1 = cos(-pi)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q8(b); book p153 = PDF p180; all branches verified

questions.knowledgeNote: tan3 = (tan+tan2)/(1-tan.tan2): the equation becomes tan3.tan.tan2 = 0 - then throw out every point where a tan is undefined (none of n.pi/3 is one).
questions.question: Q8(c). Solve tantheta + tan2theta = tan3theta [T.U. 2057 S].
questions.solution: With T = tan+tan2: T = T/(1-tan.tan2), so T.tan.tan2 = 0. tan = 0: t = k.pi. tan2 = 0: t = k.pi/2 (odd k undefined for tan, even k already counted). T = 0: sin3/(cos.cos2) = 0 gives 3t = n.pi, t = n.pi/3 (all keep every tan defined: n.pi/3 = pi/2+k.pi and = pi/4+k.pi/2 have no integer solutions). Union: t = n.pi/3. Verified at 0, pi/3, 2pi/3. (Key line illegible; answer substitution-verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q8(c) [T.U. 2057 S]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); definedness checked, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: 2sinxsin3x = cos2x-cos4x: then cos2x(1-2cos2x) = 0.
questions.question: Q8(d). Solve 2sinx.sin3x = 1 [T.U. 2052 H].
questions.solution: cos2x-cos4x = 1 gives cos2x(1-2cos2x) = 0 (using cos4x = 2cos^2 2x-1). cos2x = 0: x = n.pi +- pi/4. cos2x = 1/2: x = n.pi +- pi/6. Verified: x = pi/4 gives 2(.707)(.707) = 1; x = pi/6 gives 2(.5)(1) = 1. Matches the key: '(4n+-1).pi/4, (6n+-1).pi/6'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q8(d) [T.U. 2052 H]; book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cosec^2-1 = cot^2: (cosec-2)(cosec+1) = 0.
questions.question: Q9(a). Solve cot^2x - cosecx - 1 = 0.
questions.solution: cosec^2x-cosecx-2 = (cosecx-2)(cosecx+1) = 0. cosecx = 2: x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6. cosecx = -1: x = (4n-1).pi/2. Verified: x = -pi/2 gives 0+1-1 = 0. Matches the key.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q9(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Square it: cosx(cosx+4/5)... then KEEP only branches satisfying 2cosx+1 = sinx - here both survive.
questions.question: Q9(b). Solve 2cosx + 1 = sinx.
questions.solution: (2cosx+1)^2 = sin^2x gives 5cos^2x+4cosx = cosx(5cosx+4) = 0. cosx = 0: x = 2n.pi+pi/2 (check: 1 = 1 valid; 2n.pi-pi/2 gives 1 = -1 rejected). cosx = -4/5: then sinx = -3/5, i.e. x = 2n.pi+pi+alpha with sin(alpha) = 3/5 (check: -8/5+1 = -3/5 valid). Solutions: x = 2n.pi+pi/2 or 2n.pi+pi+alpha. (Key partially legible; every kept branch substitution-verified, rejects verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q9(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); extraneous branch rejected

questions.knowledgeNote: sinx/cos^2x = sqrt(2): quadratic in sinx with roots 1/sqrt(2) and -sqrt(2) - keep only |.| <= 1.
questions.question: Q9(c). Solve secx.tanx = sqrt(2).
questions.solution: sinx = sqrt(2)cos^2x = sqrt(2)(1-sin^2x) gives sqrt(2)sin^2x+sinx-sqrt(2) = 0: sinx = 1/sqrt(2) (other root -sqrt(2) rejected). x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/4. Verified: x = pi/4 gives sqrt(2).1 = sqrt(2). (Statement via image read: product, not sum.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q9(c); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); |sin|<=1 enforced

questions.knowledgeNote: sin^4 = (1-cos2x)^2/4: the cos^2 2x terms cancel leaving 1-2cos2x = 0.
questions.question: Q9(d). Solve 4sin^4x - cos^2 2x = 0.
questions.solution: (1-cos2x)^2-cos^2 2x = 1-2cos2x = 0, so cos2x = 1/2: x = n.pi +- pi/6 (=(6n+-1).pi/6). Verified: x = pi/6 gives 4/16-1/4 = 0. Matches the key. (Statement via image read: 4sin^4x.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q9(d); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin8theta = 8sinthetacostheta...: 4cos.cos2.cos4 = sin8/(2sin) - zeros at n.pi/8 except multiples of pi.
questions.question: Q10(a). Solve costheta + cos3theta + cos5theta + cos7theta = 0.
questions.solution: Pair outer/inner: 2cos4.cos3+2cos4.cos = 2cos4(cos3+cos) = 4cos.cos2.cos4 = sin8/(2sin) = 0 (sin != 0). So sin8 = 0, sin != 0: theta = n.pi/8 with n not a multiple of 8; i.e. (4n+-1).pi/8, (4n+-1).pi/4, (4n+-1).pi/2 families. Matches the key's three-family form.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q10(a); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: T(1-tan.tan2) = T with T = tan+tan2: T.tan.tan2 = 0 - union of tan = 0 and tan+tan2 = 0 is just n.pi/3.
questions.question: Q10(b). Solve tantheta + tan2theta + tan3theta = 0.
questions.solution: tan3 = (tan+tan2)/(1-tan.tan2) gives (tan+tan2).tan.tan2 = 0. tan = 0: t = k.pi. tan2 = 0: t = k.pi/2 (odd k undefined for tan, even k already counted). tan+tan2 = sin3/(cos.cos2) = 0: 3t = n.pi, t = n.pi/3 (all keep every tan defined: no integer n hits pi/2+k.pi or pi/4+k.pi/2). Union: t = n.pi/3. Verified at 0, pi/3 (sqrt(3)-sqrt(3)+0 = 0), 2pi/3. (Key line illegible; substitution-verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q10(b); book p153 = PDF p180 (image read); definedness checked, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: (t^2-3)/t = 2tan3theta with t = tantheta: clears to (t^2-1)(t^2-3) = 0 - then check all 8 against tan3theta's undefined points (none hit).
questions.question: Q11. Find all solutions of tantheta - 3cottheta = 2tan3theta between 0deg and 360deg.
questions.solution: (t^2-3)/t = 2(3t-t^3)/(1-3t^2) clears to t^4-4t^2+3 = (t^2-1)(t^2-3) = 0: tantheta = +-1, +-sqrt(3). In [0, 360): 45, 135, 225, 315 (from +-1) and 60, 120, 240, 300 (from +-sqrt(3)). Domain check: none equals 30+60k (tan3 undefined) or 90k (tan/cot undefined). All 8 valid. (Key garbled; every value substitution-verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q11; book p153-154 = PDF p180 (image read); domain-checked

questions.knowledgeNote: Two equations, two unknowns: tanx+tany = sin(x+y)/(cosxcosy) = 2 with cosxcosy = 1/2 forces sin(x+y) = 1.
questions.question: Q12. Find the (principal) solution of tanx + tany = 2, 2cosxcosy = 1 (general solution not required).
questions.solution: cosxcosy = 1/2 and (tanx+tany) = sin(x+y)/(cosxcosy) = 2 gives sin(x+y) = 1, so x+y = pi/2 (principal). Then tany = cotx and tanx+cotx = 2 gives (tanx-1)^2 = 0: tanx = 1, x = pi/4, y = pi/4. Check: 1+1 = 2; 2(1/2) = 1. Solution: (pi/4, pi/4).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Ex 4.2 Q12; book p154 = PDF p180 (image read); verified pair

questions.knowledgeNote: tanA+tanB+tanC = tanAtanBtanC iff A+B+C = k.pi: here 6theta = k.pi, minus odd k (tan3theta undefined there).
questions.question: Q13(i). Solve tantheta + tan2theta + tan3theta = tantheta.tan2theta.tan3theta.
questions.solution: Holds iff theta+2theta+3theta = k.pi (all tans defined), i.e. 6theta = k.pi: theta = k.pi/6. Exclude odd k (tan3theta = tan(k.pi/2) undefined) and k = 3 mod 6 (tantheta undefined; already odd). Even k: theta = m.pi/3. Verified: pi/3 gives 0 = 0; 0 gives 0 = 0. questions.knowledgeNote: Clear denominators: -(t^3)+3t^2+3t... factors as (t+1)(t^2-4t+1) = 0 - three tan values: -1, 2+-sqrt(3) = tan(-45, 15, 75 deg).
questions.question: Q13(ii). Solve tantheta + tan2theta + tantheta.tan2theta = 1.
questions.solution: With t = tantheta: t+2t/(1-t^2)+2t^2/(1-t^2) = 1 clears to t^3-3t^2-3t+1 = (t+1)(t^2-4t+1) = 0. t = -1: theta = n.pi-pi/4. t = 2+sqrt(3) = tan75: theta = n.pi+5pi/12. t = 2-sqrt(3) = tan15: theta = n.pi+pi/12. All verified (e.g. pi/12: (2-sqrt(3))+1/sqrt(3)+(2-sqrt(3))/sqrt(3) = 1).

questions.question: Q13(iii). Solve tan(pi/4+theta) + tan(pi/4-theta) = 4.
questions.solution: 2(1+t^2)/(1-t^2) = 4 where t = tantheta, so t^2 = 1/3: tantheta = +-1/sqrt(3), theta = n.pi +- pi/6 (t = +-1 never hits the excluded 1). Verified: pi/6 gives tan(5pi/12)+tan(pi/12) = (2+sqrt(3))+(2-sqrt(3)) = 4. (Statement via image read.)

questions.knowledgeNote: (sin2x-1)(tanx-1) = 0: BOTH branches give x = n.pi+pi/4 - a double lock.
questions.question: Q14(i). Solve sin2x.tanx + 1 = sin2x + tanx [T.U. 2051 H, 058 S].
questions.solution: (sin2x-1)(tanx-1) = 0. sin2x = 1: x = n.pi+pi/4. tanx = 1: x = n.pi+pi/4. So x = n.pi+pi/4 (cos != 0 throughout). Verified: sin(pi/2).1+1 = 2 = 1+1. Matches the key: 'n.pi+pi/4'.

questions.knowledgeNote: (tanx-1)(2sinx-1) = 0: two independent families.
questions.question: Q14(ii). Solve 2sinx.tanx + 1 = tanx + 2sinx [T.U. 2053 H].
questions.solution: (tanx-1)(2sinx-1) = 0. tanx = 1: x = n.pi+pi/4. sinx = 1/2: x = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6. Both verified (e.g. pi/6: 2(.5)(1/sqrt(3))+1 = 1/sqrt(3)+1 = tan+2sin). Matches the key.

questions.knowledgeNote: cosx-cos2x = sin2x-sinx: -2sin(3x/2)sin(-x/2) = 2cos(3x/2)sin(x/2).
questions.question: Q15(i). Solve cosx + sinx = cos2x + sin2x.
questions.solution: 2sin(x/2)(sin(3x/2)-cos(3x/2)) = 0. sin(x/2) = 0: x = 2n.pi. tan(3x/2) = 1: x = (4n+1).pi/6. Verified: pi/6 gives (sqrt(3)+1)/2 on both sides. Matches the key: '2n.pi, (4n+1).pi/6'.

questions.question: Q15(ii). Solve cosx - sinx = cos(alpha) + sin(alpha).
questions.solution: -2sin((x+alpha)/2)sin((x-alpha)/2) = 2sin((x+alpha)/2)cos((x-alpha)/2), i.e. 2sin((x+alpha)/2)(-sin((x-alpha)/2)-cos((x-alpha)/2)) = 0. sin((x+alpha)/2) = 0: x = 2n.pi-alpha. tan((x-alpha)/2) = -1: x = 2n.pi+alpha-pi/2. Verified at alpha = 0: {2n.pi} and {2n.pi-pi/2} both satisfy cosx-sinx = 1. (Statement via image read; key fragment '2n.pi+-alpha' appears to drop the -pi/2.)
